source.objectiveEnglish: ask what is fresh, filled, sweet, savory, or typical
source.roleplayEnglish: Ask the server to explain three pastries and recommend one made that morning.

archivedDraft.scene: At a bakery café, Sam asks about three pastries without inventing what they contain.

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Common Mexican term for sweet pastries in general.
Can also mean cake, depending on the country.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 今日作ったものはどれですか。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Which one is the most typical?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: どれがいちばん代表的ですか。
中に何か入っていますか。
甘いですか、それとも塩気のあるものですか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Is it sweet or something savory/salty?

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Which one came out of the oven today?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 今日焼き上がったのはどれですか。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Un viajero entra a una panadería en la mañana.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: A traveler walks into a bakery in the morning.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 朝、旅行者がパン屋に入ります。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: In the morning, a traveler enters a bread shop.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Hay muchos panes y pasteles en el mostrador.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: There are many breads and pastries on the counter.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カウンターには、たくさんのパンとペストリーが並んでいます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: There are many breads and pastries lined up on the counter.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: He asks: What is fresh today?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は「今日作ったものはどれですか」と尋ねます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler asks which items were made today.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La empleada dice que el pan dulce es de esta mañana.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The employee says the sweet bread is from this morning.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員は、パン・ドゥルセは今朝のものだと言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The employee says that the pan dulce is from this morning.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The traveler asks: Which one is filled?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は「中に何か入っているのはどれですか」と尋ねます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler asks which one has something inside.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Ella explica que la concha es dulce y la empanada es salada.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: She explains that the concha is sweet and the empanada is savory.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員は、コンチャは甘く、エンパナーダは塩気のあるものだと説明します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The employee explains that the concha is sweet and the empanada is savory/salty.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Él dice: Quiero probar algo típico de aquí.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: He says: I want to try something typical from here.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は「この辺で一般的なものを食べてみたいです」と言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler says that they want to try something common to this area.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La empleada recomienda un bolillo con queso.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The employee recommends a bolillo with cheese.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員はボリージョとチーズの組み合わせをすすめます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The employee recommends a combination of bolillo and cheese.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El viajero pide una concha y un café, por favor.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The traveler orders a concha and a coffee, please.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は「コンチャを一つとコーヒーを一杯、お願いします」と注文します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler orders one concha and one cup of coffee, please.

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Ask which bakery items were prepared today, whether one has a filling, and what staff recommend; preserve the Mexican bakery item names as vocabulary.
speakingGoalCandidate: Ask the server to explain three pastries and recommend one made that morning.
sourceConflictInternal: Core 3 source names no city or country. Its word notes identify pan dulce and bolillo as Mexican terms. The roleplay asks a server to explain three pastries and recommend one made that morning, but the Reader explains only concha and empanada, never says the recommended bolillo was made that morning, and ends with an order for concha. The filled-item question is answered with sweet versus savory, not a filling. The archived Japanese draft adds Sam, anpan, bean paste and cheese bread, and recommends the listed croissant instead of the source bolillo. These differences need source/locale review before release.

sourceActorsInternal: Spanish Reader uses a male traveler and a female employee; Japanese narration uses neutral nouns. No audio casting decision is made.
reviewQuestionsInternal: Resolve the roleplay-versus-Reader gap about three pastry explanations and a recommendation made that morning; source setting is an unnamed bakery.
The Reader question about a filling receives a sweet-versus-savory answer; decide whether to correct the source before any learner answer is selected.
Confirm Japanese spellings for pan dulce, bolillo, concha and empanada with a qualified Japanese and Mexican-food reviewer.
Decide whether 今日作った preserves fresh today, distinct from the separate oven question, without overclaiming just baked.
Resolve pastry/pastel, savory/salado, filling/中身 and typical/代表的 in context.
Confirm the bolillo-with-cheese serving relation without inventing a filling.
